card.name: Mendiani
card.era: Traditional; featured in Les Ballets Africains from the 1950s
card.tagline: Malinke initiation dance for a chosen young girl dancer
card.profile: Mendiani (Mandiani, Manjani) is a social dance of the Malinke (Maninka) people of Upper Guinea - especially the Siguiri region - and Mali (ethnomusicology citing Eric Charry; Mande Drum and Dance). Traditionally a chosen pre-pubescent girl, regarded as the village's best dancer, is initiated into the Mendiani society; she relinquishes the title at puberty and chooses a successor. Carried on young men's shoulders to the rhythm Denadon while wearing a large boubou and mask, she removes them as the drummers switch to Mendiani and performs highly acrobatic, graceful steps to djembe and dunun (Mande Drum and Dance; pancocojams).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologist Eric Charry notes Mendiani is 'associated with young girl dancers in upper Guinea (the region of Siguiri especially)', usually cited as the tradition's source, just as Kouroussa is cited for Dundunba (Cuyahoga CC / Charry).
